reasons: The PromQL applies a literal `100 *` scale that is not in the Datadog source. The rules forbid applying unit scales in promql; the percent-vs-ratio conversion belongs in notes with a documentation link.

Aggregation differs: Datadog takes max across hosts of each host's CPU-averaged iowait percent, while the candidate averages across all CPU series of all hosts first and then takes max of that single value, which is effectively just the global average.

Unit differs: Datadog system.cpu.iowait is a percent gauge (0-100), while system.cpu.time is cumulative seconds, so the candidate's value is a derived wait fraction rather than the same quantity in the same unit.
Grouping and series: both sides yield one series with no by-clause, but the candidate's inner avg collapses per-host structure before the max, so the per-host-then-max semantics are lost.

Metric choice is defensible (cpu_mode="wait" matches the observed label cpu_mode), but the derivation from cumulative CPU time is not an exact OTel equivalent of the Datadog gauge, so the request should be reviewed against the mapping rules.
